title: Aliases
text: Aliases Client-side command shortcuts — not Powermud’s in-game alias command. Commands Input Action /alias NAME EXPANSION Create or replace an alias /unalias NAME Remove an alias /aliases List all aliases /aliases filter List aliases whose name or body matches filter Names are one word, case-insensitive. Expansions can be several MUD commands. Expansion features Chains — separate commands with ; (e.g. look;score ). Trailing args — a one-word alias can take the rest of the line ( /alias bs backstab → bs orc sends backstab orc ). Prefix args — name the alias NAME $1$ and use $1$ in the body for the words after the command (e.g. /alias ca $1$ cast stoneskin on $1$ ). Nesting — aliases can call other aliases; cycles return an error instead of looping. zScript — bodies containing # run a small Mudlet-style subset (limited timing and action lines). Special “smart alias” marker strings from other clients are not supported here — those expansions are blocked for safety. Autocomplete Type / in the command field to suggest client slash commands and your alias names. While typing /alias … or /unalias … , alias autocomplete hides so you are not interrupted. Storage Aliases live in this browser’s localStorage under playpowermud-aliases . They do not sync across devices or browsers. Use Export config / Import config on the play page to back up aliases, comms, skin, and your learned map. Powermud’s own saved aliases (if any) are separate — use this client’s /alias for playpowermud. Examples /alias cma cast magic invulnerability /alias bs backstab /alias ca $1$ cast stoneskin on $1$;cast bless on $1$ /alias esetcolors eset ansi on;eset tell bold blue;eset say green Then type ca bishop or esetcolors like ordinary commands (no leading / ).

title: Bastion of High Sorcery
headings: From the well to the Bastion
text: Bastion of High Sorcery The Bastion is Powermud's guild of general wizards, with seven schools of magic including Enchantment and Illusion, plus scribing. Getting in is a small quest of its own: first you have to find the guild, then bring its doorkeeper a gift. This page tells the story of how we did it. Hints start vague and get stronger, and anything that gives the answer away is hidden. Click a Spoiler bar to reveal it. Contents Who can join Finding the Bastion The price of entry Finding the Golden Amulet A trap in the well From the well to the Bastion Joining Who can join Races Minimum stats Where Human, Elf, Half-Elf Int 15, Wis 13 A moving tower in the forests west of Threshold (a second mirror is rumoured south of Elinost) Like most guilds, you need about 500 exp before you can join. Our character was an elf from the Adventurer's Guild with just over 500 exp. If you want to restat , do it before you join a guild. It only works in the Adventurer's Guild. See Stats, restat and hometowns . A mage guild can lose fighting skills such as Slash. Read help bastion in game before you commit. Joining is hard to undo. Finding the Bastion The Bastion doesn't have a front door in any town. Its way in is through a mirror. Hint 1: Leave Threshold to the west, past the guard at the forest's edge, and follow the forest trails away from the Caravan Route. Pay attention when a room description mentions something strange off in the distance. Hint 2: You're looking for a black tower that has no business being in the middle of the woods. Squirrels will scold you as you get close. Spoiler: where the tower is Spoiler: getting through the mirror The price of entry Inside the Bastion, look around the meeting hall. The mage who decides who gets in won't do it for free. Spoiler: who to talk to, and what he wants Finding the Golden Amulet Hint 1: The doorkeeper's hint is exact. The amulet is under Threshold, in a well, and not in the catacombs. Most of the town gets its water from newer wells. Hint 2: Look in Threshold's roughest, darkest alley. One stretch of it is "somewhat more lit" than the rest. Hint 3: Going down is harder than pressing d . Try spelling out what you want to do with the well. Hint 4: At the bottom, don't go looking for passages. Look closely at the well itself. Its walls are packed stone and mortar. Spoiler: where the well is Spoiler: getting down the well Spoiler: getting the amulet (full answer) A trap in the well Low-level characters: be careful at the bottom of the well. There's something there you can trigger by accident, and it drops you somewhere you really don't want to be. Read the next spoiler if you'd rather not find out the hard way. Spoiler: the metal plate From the well to the Bastion With the amulet in hand, head back to the tower. Spoiler: full walking route, well bottom to the mirror Joining Take the amulet back to the mage who asked for it. He should let you in, as long as your abilities are high enough. TODO (Spencer): fill in how the handover went: the exact command used to give the amulet, what he said, the join message, and anything the guild hands out to new members. We haven't recorded the "abilities high enough" check either, so it's still unconfirmed. Spoiler: the handover From our own play on Nov 3, 2026. Powermud changes over time, and the game itself is always right. Check help bastion and help guilds in game.

title: Beginner's guide
text: Powermud Beginner's Guide How to start, survive, level, make money and stay out of trouble in Powermud, with an overview of all 12 races and 24 guilds. Tips from other players are marked as unverified. Contents What Powermud is Your first hour Essential commands Reading your prompt Races Stats, restat and hometowns Guilds Which race for which guild Professions Drow houses and Bey-Sandrax Combat basics Healing and resting Death and getting lost Training skills Where to hunt Getting around Money, selling and gear Dangers to avoid Community and etiquette Tips to explore What Powermud is Powermud is a fantasy LPMud that has been running since 1993. You play it by typing commands in a text world of cities, dungeons and wilderness, with two dozen guilds, professions, magic and other players. Server: powermud.com port 2000 (telnet, no SSL) Clients: Any MUD client works, for example Mudlet, MUSHclient, TinTin++ or Blightmud. New account: Type a new user name at the login prompt, then create <name> . Names are letters only. Fresh start: Every old character was archived on 25 Oct 2026, so everyone is new. Colour: Turn ANSI on. If tells and says look wrong, use eset to fix the colours. Your first hour Create your character. Choose a race that fits the guild you want later (see Which race for which guild). 'none' is accepted for the real name and email questions. Gear up with Pete. You start in the Newbie Arena. say equip me gets you a torch, leather armour, a small dagger, mace and sword, and 50 drakaan. Wear and wield two weapons. wear all , then wield two weapons. Sword trains slash, mace blunt, dagger pierce. Pick the skill your future guild keeps. Get blessed. say bless me . Ask again when you see 'You lose your blessed feeling.' Use say heal me when you're hurt. You have to say these. Fight rats. Go north and kill rat . Afterwards, get all from corpse and optionally bury corpse . Train. skills shows your skills, cost shows prices and train all at Pete raises them. A new character can go from 1 to almost 500 exp in about 20 minutes. Try the Academy. The official newbie guide points to the PowerMud Academy, down and north from Pete, for free exp and coins. Leave at 500 exp. At 500 exp the arena moves you out. Use restat first if you want it, then find a guild. Don't fight outside the arena yet. Brand-new characters who fight outside the arena will probably be killed. Essential commands Command What it does look / l at <thing> Room description, or a closer look at an object. Read every room: hidden exits are hinted there. score / sscore Your stats, exp, hometown, alignment and wealth i / equip Inventory, and what you're wearing and wielding skills / skills -p Your skill levels and skill exp effects Your active buffs and their strength who / finger <name> Who's online (ghosts show [ GHOST! ]), and info on one player kill <mob> / flee Start a fight, or try to run wimpy Automatic flee threshold. 40% is a good setting. gauge <npc> Rates an NPC's skills, not how dangerous it is judge <item> Rates a weapon or armour, for example at Willen Noggler's in Threshold rest now / wake / stand Resting trance for fast SP. You have to wake and stand afterwards. list / buy / sell all Shop or waiter menu, buying, and selling everything you carry that isn't worn uptime / time How long the MUD has been up (used for respawns), and day or night (some shops close at night) quests list / quests breakdown Open quests and the exp each one recommends homeland Teleports you to your hometown, but only at 4,000 exp or less help <topic> / guildhelp In-game help. Try help newbie , help races , help guilds , help <guild> , help professions , help alignment . alias <name> <cmds> Your own shortcuts. Separate commands with ; , for example alias cb medallion bless . secure <item> Toggles [SECURE] so you don't sell or drop it by accident Reading your prompt An example prompt: [HP: 600(600(100%)) SP: 62(200(31%)) XP: 21270(730(36%)) Cash: 885(29370)] HP: Current (max (percent)). Constitution and total exp raise your max. SP: Spell or skill points. Openers like assassinate cost 5. Below about 3 you get 'too fatigued', so rest. XP: Total experience, followed by a progress counter that shrinks as you gain exp. Total exp decides your title, max HP, guild joining (500), item save levels (1,000 for magic gear) and homeland (4,000 or less). Cash: Drakaan you're carrying (drakaan in the bank) Races From the in-game race help files. 'Experienced' races are flagged by the game as for experienced players only. Race Above average Below average Resistances Human Nothing Nothing None Elf Int, Dex Str, Con Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (medium), Dragonfear (low) Half-Elf Wis Cha Enchant (high), Illusion (low) Drow (experienced) Int, Dex Str, Con Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (low), Dragonfear (medium) Gnome Int Str, Wis Enchant (very high), Illusion (very high) Svirfneblin (experienced) Int Cha Enchant (very high), Illusion (very high) Dwarf Str, Con Int, Cha Enchant (high), Illusion (low), Poison (medium), Dragonfear (medium) Duergar (experienced) Str, Con Int, Cha Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (medium), Poison (medium), Dragonfear (medium) Halfling Dex, Cha Str, Wis None listed Half-Orc Str, Con Int, Cha Dragonfear (low) Half-Ogre Str, Con (exceptional) Int, Wis, Cha (exceptionally low), Dex Dragonfear (high) Minotaur (experienced) Str (exceptional), Con Wis, Cha (very low) Dragonfear (high) Human — Average at everything and the widest guild choice of any race (13 guilds, including Knights, Monks, Northmen and Battlemages). The safest pick for a first character. Elf — Good and nature-loving; home city Elinost and the Great Forest. Natural infravision. Joins the Elite, Priests of Eli, Bastion and Rangers. Half-Elf — Mixes with both races; the second-widest guild list (10), from Militia to Bastion to Battlemages. Drow — Purely evil Underdark elves of Nal Shaddar who worship Loth and hate elves. They see in the dark without light, and drow belong to noble houses. Guilds split by gender: males Melee-Magthere, females Arach-Tillith. Gnome — Tinkers and gem-cutters with very high illusion resistance; natural Illusionists. Svirfneblin — Deep gnomes of the Underdark, good miners, mostly with illusionist talent. Dwarf — Stout warriors who love gold and hate orcs and goblins. Natural Stronghold Honor Guard, also Church of Kertaine. Duergar — Evil, half-mad Underdark dwarves of Dunkrist, sometimes allied with drow. Homeguard or Dark Trinity. Halfling — High Dex makes picking locks, pockets and hiding easy. Thief, Assassin, Merchant, Church or Rangers. Half-Orc — Strong outcasts; a solid fit for Militia, Battlemages, Cult or Assassin. Half-Ogre — The strongest and toughest race, with the weakest minds; tends toward evil. Militia, Cult, Disciples, Thief or Assassin. Minotaur — Sea-faring bull-men. Only special helmets fit over the horns. Mariner is their own guild; Battlemages also take them. Infravision: elves have it naturally, and Underdark races (drow, duergar, svirfneblin) see better in the dark than an elf. The Alteration spell Infravision gives elf-level dark vision to anyone. Alignment is Good, Neutral or Evil and shifts with what you kill: killing something of your own alignment pushes you toward the opposite. score shows it. Monks are strongest when neutral. Some cities' NPCs attack certain races on sight, so check how a city treats your race before walking in. Stats, restat and hometowns Stat Average What it does Constitution 12 HP, and how fast HP grows. 'Vitally important to everyone.' Strength 11 Damage, carrying weight, doors and obstacles Dexterity 11 Dodging, reacting to surprises, ranged accuracy Intelligence 10 Higher-level spells, casting checks, seeing through illusions Wisdom 11 Resistance to magical attack Charisma - Shop prices when haggling; some creatures react badly to low Charisma restat only works in the Adventurer's Guild, with at least 1 exp, before you join a guild, at 900 exp or less, and at most 3 times. It shows your race's stat ranges. Set it to beat your target guild's minimums. Hometowns: Kalinport, Deepwater and Threshold, plus Jaarmin Keep, Dunagin and Zahkar for advanced players. Pick one near your guild, because homeland takes you there. Some hometowns grant special abilities, and you can change hometown later. Guilds From the in-game guild help files and the official site. Join at 500+ exp (Merchants are the exception); at the recruiter, type info for the joining task. Members pay less for most Threshold services. An easy first guild for a human-ish fighter. Knights of Nereka — Mounted knights with riding, lancing, shield bash, triple attack and advanced defense. Three orders (Circle, Blade, Kingfisher); the top order gets clerical spells from Kertaine. The knighthood distrusts non-clerical magic. Elinost Elite — Guards of the Speaker of the Moon. Advanced melee, dual and offhand, plus hide and sneak. Stronghold Honor Guard — Dwarven defenders with dual, triple, offhand and advanced melee. Dunkrist Homeguard — Ambush fighters: backstab, dual, unarmed dual and triple, and epic slash, blunt and unarmed. Join by bringing the quill pen from the Receiving Clerk at the Dunagin docks. Spells include Burning Hands (10 SP), Shocking Grasp (15), Fireball (45) and Blade Circle (60). title: Comms
text: Comms panel Tells, room says, and shouts in a side panel — guild chat and announce lines stay in the main log. Open the panel Alt + C ( Option+C on macOS) toggles expand/collapse. On mobile, tap Comms in the bottom bar. What gets captured Tells — incoming and your outgoing tells Says — room speech (yours always; others only if they are in the client’s known-player list) Shouts — always shown Each line has a timestamp. The panel keeps up to 400 recent entries. Powermud channels ( [guild] , group chat, fields, etc.) are not copied into this panel — read them in the main terminal (use eset colors from Terminal & colors ). Per character When the logged-in character changes, the comms list switches to that character’s saved history in localStorage on this browser. Nothing syncs across devices. If a tell or say is missing here, check the main log — parsing waits for a full line, and some lines are filtered (e.g. replay blocks, announce spam).

title: Getting started
headings: What is not in this client
text: Getting started Connect from the home page, play in one tab, reconnect when the relay drops. What this client is Play Powermud is a browser client for Powermud: a terminal, personal aliases, a comms log, and a world map in one tab. Everything except the network relay runs in your browser; aliases and comms preferences use localStorage , and map discoveries use IndexedDB on this device. Keyboard shortcuts On macOS, Alt is labeled Option . Shortcuts use Alt , not Option+Command . Shortcut Action Alt + W Toggle wiki overlay Alt + M Toggle world map panel Alt + C Toggle comms panel Alt + D Focus terminal: scroll log to bottom and focus the command line Connect Open / and click Connect . Log in on Powermud as usual (name, password). The password field is masked in the UI. Use the command line at the bottom; ↑/↓ recall history. Empty Enter repeats the last command. The site talks to Powermud through a relay at /api/ws — a dumb pipe to powermud.com:2000 . You cannot point the public relay at another host from the browser; only the server config chooses the target. Wiki while you play Click Wiki in the header (or press Alt + W ) to open help and game reference in an overlay on top of the client. Your MUD connection stays open underneath — close the wiki or press Escape to return to the terminal (new output appears when you close; text you missed while reading is not replayed). Session length (Vercel) On Vercel, the WebSocket closes when the function hits its max duration (about 5 minutes on Hobby, longer on Pro). When the relay drops, your character goes link-dead and you will see the login prompt again after reconnect. For long uninterrupted sessions, run your own relay: yarn relay # standalone relay; set PORT, MUD_HOST, MUD_PORT Build or load the client with RELAY_URL=wss://your-host/api/ws , or add ?relay=wss://… to the page URL for a quick test. Run locally yarn install yarn dev # http://localhost:3000 — static site + relay at /api/ws Run yarn build before deploy; Vercel serves public/ and deploys the relay function. Optional environment (hosting) Variable Default Meaning MUD_HOST / MUD_PORT powermud.com / 2000 Relay target ALLOWED_ORIGINS (any) Comma-separated origins allowed to open the relay RELAY_URL this site’s /api/ws Build-time: external relay URL for the client What is not in this client Play Powermud is intentionally simple: no auto-walking, speedwalk, click-to-walk on the map, trigger scripts, imported “smart” alias packs, or saved login profiles. You send each command yourself from the command line. Next steps Terminal & colors — eset after login Aliases — macros in this browser World map — where you are in the world graph

title: Quest system
text: Quest system From in-game help quests (2026-10-19). Commands Command Purpose quests list Available quests quests completed Finished quests quests breakdown Quest points (QP) breakdown with recommended exp minimums Also: help quest points for how QP affects experience. Quest lists and hooks (not walkthroughs): Quests corpus . Rules (paraphrased) Quest points are awarded only if you finish the entire quest yourself, in order , without logging off mid-quest. Markers reset on logout or death; reboot breaks quests too. Sharing quest information with other players is not allowed (including paid help or cross-guild spell-ups for quest fights). Do not be hidden/invis when giving items to quest NPCs — they will not see you and keep the item . Quest points grant an experience bonus on kills. Quest progress is fragile: logging out, dying, or a reboot can reset markers. Plan uninterrupted time before starting a chain.

title: Quests corpus

Clues (hooks only) These are starting points from play logs — not full walkthroughs (quest terms of service discourage sharing complete solutions). title: Races & stats
text: Player races & abilities From in-game help races and selected race help (pulled 2026-10-30). All playable races help races lists: drow, duergar, dwarf, elf, half-elf, halfling, half-orc, half-ogre, human, gnome, minotaur, svirfneblin Battlemage-eligible: Human, Half-Elf, Half-Orc, Minotaur — see Celtian Battlemages for guild requirements. Exact per-race stat rolls are shown by restat in the Adventurer Guild, not in help files. Human Advantages / disadvantages: none (baseline race). Short-lived compared to other races; generalist adventurers. Half-elf Above average Wisdom; below average Charisma. Resistances: Enchant (high), Illusion (low). Half-orc Above average Strength and Constitution; below average Intelligence and Charisma. Resistance: Dragonfear (low). Minotaur Very high Strength, above average Constitution; very low Wisdom and Charisma. Resistance: Dragonfear (high). Horned — special helmet types only. Marked for experienced Powermud players in help. Core abilities ( help abilities ) Stat Typical avg Role Intelligence 10 Memory, spell access; high Int may pierce illusions Constitution 12 Hit points — “vitally important” Wisdom 11 Magical resistance Strength 11 Carry weight, melee damage, doors Dexterity 11 Reaction, ranged accuracy, dodging Underdark player races (common in travel docs): drow, duergar, svirfneblin — see help drow , etc. for full text.

title: Spoilers & sources
text: Spoilers & sources Much of this wiki comes from years of player notes bundled with old Powermud downloads. Some material is spoiler-heavy or unofficial — we summarize carefully and leave the worst offenders offline. Not published here Open proxy lists tied to character names and similar “multi-connection” cheat sheets stay out of the public wiki on purpose. Spoilers and min-max notes Full quest walkthroughs ( quests.txt , psionics quest notes, and similar) Drop lists and fast-exp mob shortlists Battlemage join path (quill from Dunagin clerk) — on Battlemages , not in official help Unofficial or outdated Third-party MUD client archives, internal function name dumps, and very old doctor text files may disagree with today’s Powermud. Prefer current in-game help and the curated pages linked from Professions . Good starting points Pulled help topics, quest clues (not full solutions), explored map data, and staff name lists for social context.

title: Terminal & colors
text: Terminal & colors xterm.js output with full ANSI — Powermud eset colors render as the MUD sends them. Command line History — ↑ and ↓ walk previous commands (plain arrows, not modified). Repeat — Enter on an empty line resends the last command. Password — input is masked while Powermud asks for your password. Line cursor — ←/→ move within the line; Alt +←/→ insert telnet cursor-move sequences at the caret. Log cursor — Alt + Shift +arrow sends cursor keys to the MUD (for full-screen editors on the game side). Word delete — Alt +Backspace deletes the word before the caret (macOS Option+Backspace). Back to terminal — Alt + D scrolls the log to the bottom and focuses input ( shortcut list ). Mobile On small screens, quick buttons for look , who , and score appear above the input; Map and Comms toggle the side panels. Theme Skin: Dark / Light on the play page (and this wiki) switches UI chrome only; MUD colors still come from ANSI. The choice is saved in localStorage . Powermud ANSI ( eset ) In-game: help ansi , help eset , help variables . Help digest: Eset & ANSI . eset ansi on — required for channel colors and combat ANSI. eset <variable> <setting> — e.g. eset tell bold blue . eunset <variable> — clear one variable. Colors: black, red, green, yellow, blue, purple, cyan, white. Effects: beep, flash, underline, normal, bold, italics, inverse (not every effect shows in every client). Suggested channel preset Define once as a client alias (see Aliases ), then run it each session: eset ansi on eset tell bold blue eset say green eset shout bold cyan eset announce bold yellow eset guild bold purple eset groupchat bold magenta eset fields green eset emote cyan Example client alias: /alias esetcolors eset ansi on;eset tell bold blue;eset say green;… — run esetcolors after each login, then verify with eset . Variable Use tell Tells you see say Room speech from others shout Shouts announce Announce channel guild Guild channel groupchat Group chat fields Fields channel emote Atmosphere / soul lines

title: Walking directions
headings: Learn your way around Powermud: directions
text: Learn your way around Powermud: directions Spencer's 2008 walking list. Routes are grouped by starting city, in the original order. Each step block is copied as written, including the original typos in the steps. The place in parentheses at the start of a block is where the route begins. Other parentheses are landmarks from the list. Phrases in asterisks, such as *pry floorboard* , are commands rather than compass moves. Safety comments from the list are repeated under each route that had one. These are old player notes. Confirm exits in game, or on your map , before you trust a path. The list itself says some Merevia areas are missing, and that Samurai Village is inaccessible. title: World map
text: World map Live mapper while you play — builds a world graph from room text, entirely in your browser. Open the map Alt + M ( Option+M on macOS) expands or collapses the panel. On mobile, tap Map . What you see Your position updates as room text arrives from the MUD. Levels — use ▲/▼ in the map toolbar to change z (up/down in the world). Follow — when on, the view stays centered on you; panning or selecting another room turns it off. Search — filter mapped rooms by title, description, tags, or NPC names. Room details — click a room for exits, contents, and links. Legend — dashed = inferred link; markers for up/down and unexplored exits. Click-drag empty map space to pan. Focus the map canvas and use arrow keys to move the selection cursor between rooms (navigation only — does not send movement commands). This client does not click-to-walk, speedwalk, or auto-path. Shipped map vs your discoveries The site ships a Powermud world graph at /data/powermud.graph.json (a community baseline). As you explore, new rooms and links merge into your local copy. If a newer shipped file arrives (newer updatedAt ), new baseline rooms are merged in without wiping what you mapped. Your learned map is saved in IndexedDB ( playpowermud database) on this browser. How mapping works (short) Each command you send is queued; each room display is matched to the command that caused it. The mapper: Identifies rooms by title, exits, and description (brief and verbose look map to the same room). Learns compass, vertical, named, and secret exits as you traverse them. Re-localizes when dead reckoning disagrees with room text, so the pin stays on the right room. Periodically heals duplicate rooms and bad links (on load and as you move). Updating the shipped graph Site deploys include public/data/powermud.graph.json . When maintainers publish a newer graph, your browser merges it if the file’s updatedAt is newer than your saved base.
